subtitle: This week in Bitcoin & Nostr news

Next difficulty adjustment ~+9.6%: the hashrate came right back

topics.title: The Dip: Half Off the Peak
topics.description: From ~$74K to a $61,946 low in four days: liquidations, loss-taking, ETF outflows, and who is still buying

slides.heading: The Dip: Half Off the Peak
slides.body: Saturday night it touched $61,946, about half off the ~$126K peak. Drag the slider to pick any day since the summer high.
slides.linkLabel: The Commoner: Did you think it was going to be easy?

slides.heading: Who's Hurting, Who's Buying
bullets: $1.78B of leveraged longs wiped out Nov 9–15
Recent buyers are underwater: short-term holders' average cost is ~$74K
Biggest loss-taking since July 13: ~25,800 BTC net (CryptoQuant)
MSCI drops Strategy and Metaplanet Nov 30: forced index selling ahead
Still buying: Strategy +485 BTC (and $228M on STRC buybacks), Twenty One +154, Strive +251

slides.heading: Did You Think It Would Be Easy?
slides.body: Marty Bent asked it this week, and I think it's the right question.
bullets: The network didn't blink: blocks kept coming, hashrate ~990 EH/s
Realized price ~$53.6K: the average coin is still in profit
Andrew Howard's reasons to stay: scarcity, a splitting world, generational change, censorship resistance, collapsing trust
Ask the room: are you buying, holding or sitting out? What would change your mind?
slides.linkLabel: The Commoner: Never going to be easy

topics.title: Security Desk: Swapped Addresses
topics.description: Ledger.com served an address swapper, Trezor's shipper leaked 27,000 home addresses, and a fleet tool redirected miners

slides.heading: Security Desk: Swapped Addresses
slides.body: None of these needed anybody's private key.
bullets: Ledger.com via Optimizely: a script swapped BTC addresses. ~$7,040 stolen
Trezor's shipper Skladon leaked ~27,000 home addresses

slides.heading: Hijacked Hash, Implants, Patches
bullets: Luxor's Commander tool sent a dozen clients' miners to an attacker on OCEAN. Luxor pays them in full
Trezor confirms implants in Safe 5s from reseller CryptoBilis. Firmware 2.13.1 blocks them. Buyers: new seed
Patch now: Core Lightning v26.06.8, LDK 0.2.8 / 0.1.14, Tor 0.4.9.17

slides.heading: What To Do
bullets: Read the full address on the device screen before you sign
Ship to a pickup point. No vendor will ever ask for your seed
Know every tool that can change your payout address
Buy hardware wallets direct from the maker
slides.body: What I'm doing after this week:

topics.title: Mining: Difficulty Down, SV2 Up
topics.description: The biggest difficulty cut since June, an instant rebound, Core Scientific's exit, and Stratum V2 at the big pools

slides.heading: Mining: Difficulty Down, SV2 Up
bullets: Difficulty −9.13% to 134.82T on Nov 14, the biggest cut since June
Then the hashrate came back: next retarget ~+9.6% (block 977,760, ~Nov 26)
Hashprice ~$28–30 per PH/day. Core Scientific leaves mining by year-end for AI hosting
Stratum V2: MARA mined its first SV2 block; Foundry USA started SV2 testing
Paraguay ends all miner power contracts Dec 31, 2027 (~944 MW)

topics.title: Bitcoin Dev: Testnet 5 Is Live
topics.description: Testnet 5's genesis block, anti-exfil signing BIPs, and a common message format for air-gapped signers

slides.heading: Bitcoin Dev: Testnet 5 Is Live
bullets: Genesis mined Nov 14, committing to mainnet block 975,744's hash. 166 blocks in the first hour
Draft BIPs (Connor Avila): anti-exfil signing, so your wallet can catch a signer leaking your key
Draft BIP: one message format for air-gapped and external signers

topics.title: Policy Corner: Finney, Keys, Courts

slides.heading: Policy Corner: Finney, Keys, Courts
slides.body: The Bitcoin Policy Institute is now the Finney Foundation for Open Technology.
bullets: Now also open-source AI, digital cash, encrypted messaging
Named for Hal Finney: PGP, and Satoshi's first bitcoin transaction

links.label: Image: Finney Foundation via Bitcoin Magazine

slides.heading: Keys, Courts and Nominees
bullets: US Treasury drafts custody for its bitcoin: self-custody plus custodians. Not your keys, at national scale
Leipzig judge: end the Movie2K trial for 40,000 BTC + €38M? Next hearing Dec 3
Nominated: Levine for Hester Peirce's SEC seat, plus two CFTC picks
Germany: customs could freeze crypto over €100K of "unclear origin", no criminal case needed

topics.title: Nostr This Week: Keys on Hardware
topics.description: A Trezor Model One signs Nostr events, email between npubs, new NIP drafts, and an app that left Nostr

slides.heading: Nostr This Week: Keys on Hardware
slides.body: A patched Trezor Model One signs Nostr events on a button press.
bullets: NIP-46 bridge for Coracle and noStrudel. Lab only
nVelope: email between npubs, encrypted to a separate key

slides.heading: New NIPs and a Breakup
bullets: NIP-402: pay a relay over Lightning (L402) inside the connection
Sjors: NIP-0D puts relay .onion addresses in DNS; NIP-1B shares signed abuse reports
Gupt 6.0.0 leaves Nostr relays with six complaints. Fair, or already being fixed?

topics.title: AI Corner: Agents Pay Their Own Way
topics.description: pi402 lets an agent buy its own inference over Lightning, x402 adds Lightning, and llama.cpp hits 1.0

slides.heading: AI Corner: Agents Pay Their Own Way
slides.body: Lightning Labs' pi402: a coding agent buys its own AI inference over Lightning, per token.
bullets: No account, no API key, no card. Per-request caps and a daily budget. MIT
x402 adds Lightning to its pay-per-API-call standard
Wallet of Satoshi agent skills: read and invoice, but every spend needs your tap

slides.heading: llama.cpp Hits v1.0.0
slides.body: The engine under most local AI goes stable.
bullets: Local AI is how I want Guard Dog's optional AI to run: on your own hardware

topics.title: Builder Spotlight: Guard Dog & Trust Issues
topics.description: My two new open-source tools: a security watchdog for your Bitcoin and Nostr stack, and Lightning on block explorers it doesn't believe

slides.heading: Builder Spotlight: Guard Dog & Trust Issues
slides.body: Two open-source tools I started this week. One idea: trust nothing you can check.
bullets: Why now: AI makes finding bugs cheap, for attackers too. 2026: Coldcard, BTCPay, Alby Hub, LNbits
Guard Dog: a watchdog for your node, relay and mint (started Nov 16, pre-alpha)
Trust Issues: Lightning without a full node, and without blind trust in one explorer (Nov 17, signet)
Built the way Super Testnet taught me: readable, runnable, no server needed

slides.heading: Guard Dog: Security That Never Sleeps
slides.body: It runs on your node or a small box at home, learns what you run and keeps checking it.
bullets: It finds Core/Knots, LND, CLN, BTCPay, mints and relays on Umbrel, StartOS, Docker…
An advisory hits something you run: you get a plain-English alert by Nostr DM, ntfy or email

slides.heading: See What an Attacker Sees
slides.body: My clickable mock-up: made-up regtest data, nothing to install.
bullets: Open ports, router mappings, Tor, plus Scout: finds Bitcoin and Nostr gear on your network
Recommends the safest version: signed, hashes match, past a cooling-off, no advisories

slides.heading: Never Holds Keys, Never Says "Secure"
bullets: It never holds your keys or moves funds. No telemetry. Nothing changes without your tap
It says "no known issues found", with when it checked and what it couldn't see
I grade it with "judges" written before the features: hostile text 48/48, leaks caught on 88 test captures
23 real advisories in, matcher next, so it honestly scores 0 of 9 today. I'd rather it tell on itself
~190 commits in two days. Next up: the first real finding, end to end

slides.heading: Trust Issues: Explorers on Trial
slides.body: It stands in for bitcoind under LND or Core Lightning, so you skip the 700+ GB download.
bullets: Asks mempool.space, Emzy's mempool and Blockstream, all over Tor
Proves what it can (proof of work, merkle roots), cross-checks the rest

slides.heading: Why One Explorer Isn't Enough
bullets: Lightning is safe only if you see a cheating close in time to punish it
One explorer could hide that block, or quietly drop your penalty transaction
So: "unspent" needs two explorers agreeing; every broadcast goes to all of them
Chain quiet for 90 min: warning. 3 hours: critical, and it stops saying "synced"
Try the browser demo: a lying explorer tries five tricks, and all five get caught

slides.heading: Tested on Signet, Not for Real Money
bullets: Core Lightning v26.06.10 and LND v0.21.8 both synced through it
A 200,000-sat channel opened and a 21,000-sat payment crossed it
I refuse mainnet in code until someone outside reviews it. Even then: small amounts only
Docker: Tor, Trust Issues and one Lightning node, nothing published to the host
I'd love help on both: testers, node runners, advisory curators, white-hat breakers

topics.title: Quick Tip: Audit Your Home Server
topics.description: One forgotten container with a default password cost a Nostr regular his Bitaxe firmware and his password manager

slides.heading: Quick Tip: Audit Your Home Server
slides.body: One forgotten container on a default password: Derek Ross lost his Bitaxe firmware and his Vaultwarden.
bullets: List everything running (docker ps -a). Delete what you don't use
Change every default password, admin panels first
Keep admin pages off the open internet: Tor, a VPN or Tailscale
Patch Linux: NoisyTCP crashes any box with an open TCP port (fixed in 6.12.117, 6.18.63, 7.3.4)
This is exactly what I'm building Guard Dog to catch
